findings_and_questions.first_contract: After two eligible one-face primary edges match and either is a wall/tower abutment, the classifier chooses WallAbutment and binding appends the other face, producing two faces. The roof audit expects exactly one face for WallAbutment and OpeningCut. The later contour code either leaves the abutment kind or changes it to OpeningCut without removing the added face; the inspected edge refit only adjusts flashing, not adjacency.
findings_and_questions.condition: Constructors and intermediate passes must complete and such a coincident primary pair must be supported/reachable. The audit discrepancy follows from that source state if it remains present when checked. No generated plan was run.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Determine whether a cross-roof joint with an abutment is an internal two-face junction or a one-face boundary contact, and express one shared topology policy consistently in binding, contour handling and audit.
relationships: Related to 059 Q-L11-1f255e4a529b1484b496 and Q-L12-daa19af99971265e71a0 roof junction/contour obligations. The original Lens 12 receipt classified TowerAbutment to WallAbutment as a possible intentional unified mode; this new observation concerns face-count consumer compatibility, not name-based category inference. No automatic alias assigned.

findings_and_questions.first_contract: The binding flashing uses tag 8, assembly ID shifted 16, 0x6000 and left edge index; the immediate drainage pass uses the identical prefix and face_index*8 for a gutter floor. For an eligible left edge index 0 bound as a Valley and adjacent to its own face 0, face 0 has at least that valley as an eligible drainage edge. The pass retains RoofFlashing and creates the face-0 floor, so their ResolvedItemIds are equal at that stage.

No runtime evidence or admitted layout proven.

findings_and_questions.first_contract: Consider three distinct eligible primary assemblies A, B and C whose single-face edges all coincide. A/B pairing appends B face to A and schedules B edge for removal. A/C is skipped because A now has two faces; B/C can still pair because B is not removed until the end, then schedules C. The final edge removal retains the A edge with A/B face references but removes B and C edge records after generating additional B/C junction geometry.
findings_and_questions.condition: This is source-level reasoning over the loops, not a generated example or execution. The constructors must succeed, no earlier matching edge diverts find(), and such a three-way coincident configuration must be admitted or require explicit rejection; any later geometry cleanup and intended nonmanifold semantics are unresolved.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Set an admitted manifold/multiway contact policy at the roof graph owner; consume matched edges once or explicitly represent/reject multiway junctions and keep solids, face references and removals coherent.
relationships: The /root/lens12_frontier READ-L12-862 already flagged adjacency expansion before deferred removal and multiway semantics as a conditional question. This is a more explicit source-state consequence of that historical question; root determines canonical alias and count. Related 059 broad roof topology queue Q-L12-daa19af99971265e71a0 remains open.

findings_and_questions.first_contract: Valley drainage uses the left edge start as inlet and end extended along delta as outlet without selecting by elevation. If end.y - start.y is at least 0.09 m, the newly created route fails the downstream strict inlet.y > outlet.y + 0.01 check: its vertical difference equals 0.10 - (end.y - start.y) - 0.08*(delta.y/length).
findings_and_questions.condition: Requires a bound valley with that orientation and rise, successful nondegenerate geometry construction, survival to audit, and no other qualifying route for the same terminal. The function admits either endpoint pairing direction and the edge producer takes face polygon order; neither proves the orientation is reachable or that the check ultimately reports an issue.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Prove upstream endpoint ordering or choose the higher endpoint as inlet and lower outlet at the owner of this route, retaining the geometry tolerance, endpoint extension and downstream terminal relationship.
relationships: Related to 059 broad roof drainage/junction obligations and older 774 NATIVE-ROOF-PPS-RAW-SOURCE-002, which inventories raw drainage sample/route coordinates; not automatically the checked-point-loss identity NATIVE-ROOF-PPS-F001.

findings_and_questions.first_contract: Each roof resolver receives the same walls slice and the enclosure adapter selects Timber if any wall is timber, else Rubble if any is rubble, else Masonry. It does not filter by roof, gable host, or replacement status, whereas the support-node search filters replaced walls. Thus a remote or replaced timber wall can determine the infill material for another roof if those wall combinations are supported.
findings_and_questions.condition: Mixed, separate and replaced wall presence and the intended material authority for each gable are not established. The explicit priority and empty-wall default may be deliberate; this is not a confirmed defect or obsolete fallback.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Confirm whether the actual gable/contact wall is material authority or the building-wide policy is intended; if local authority is required, retain the host-to-enclosure relation and define missing or mixed-host handling.
relationships: Original 059 /root/segovb L11 and /root/lens12_frontier L12 separately recorded this explicit timber/rubble/masonry priority and legitimate empty case; this does not upgrade their historical disposition or establish a new defect. Native roof raw-source inventory concerns related enclosure records, not identical authority.

findings_and_questions.condition: An applicable preexisting treatment and interface must exist, and another intervening or later pass or downstream contract may remove or tolerate the interface; these bounded reads do not prove stale accepted state or an actual error.

Reverse sorted and deduplicated right-edge removals protect against ordinary index shifting; this does not establish multiway contact correctness.
Material precedence and empty walls default are explicit source policy, not automatically a bug.
Typed RoofEdgeKind, RoofMaterial, identifiers and optional selection carry real distinctions; no wholesale primitive or enum replacement inferred.
